claim: (uncited neighbour) If 2 000 s pass without a deployment, one is forced.
issue: Evaluation forces action = 1 (line 88); training instead re-draws the agent's choice until non-zero (mtd_ai_training.py:84). The sentence is uncited; see the tay2024 row.

claim: Each deployment interval is the set value plus a random delay (exponential offset).
issue: Called as exponential_variates(interval, std) at mtd_operation.py:100 and mtd_ai_operation.py:135, so interval = loc + Exp(scale).

claim: The random delay is 0.5 s on average; 200 s is the default interval.
issue: Scale 0.5 = mean of the exponential offset; MTDScheme also defaults mtd_trigger_std=0.5 (mtd_scheme.py:17). 'simultaneous' defaults to 700 s, irrelevant here.

claim: Scan for hosts, enumerate host and scan neighbours take 5 s each, port scan 25 s, brute force 20 s.
issue: Used as fixed timeouts, no random draw (attack_operation.py:66, 75, 85, 103, 111).
Same draw for the AI scheme (mtd_ai_operation.py:135).

claim: Network: 50 hosts, 4 levels of depth, 8 subnets, 5 exposed endpoints.
issue: These are the release's defaults (also TimeNetwork, time_network.py:10). Adversarial: Tay's own MTDShield runs used other sizes (training 100 hosts, train_models.py:41; evaluation 150, e6c13c6 experiments.ipynb cell 1), so the cite supports 'the release's default', not 'what Tay ran'.

claim: Two target hosts, at the deepest level.
quote: target_layer=4, total_database=2, terminate_compromise_ratio=0.8, new_network=False): ... :param total_database: the number of database nodes used for computing DAP algorithm
issue: The release sets two database hosts (the last node ids, which gen_graph places in the deepest level: network.py:54), but uses them only for the DAP algorithm, never as targets: network_type defaults to 1, the general scenario (network.py:66), and the end-on-target code is commented out (attack_operation.py:363-367). Treating the database hosts as target hosts is the dissertation's mapping.
fix_text: "2, at the deepest level [tay2024code]" -> "2 database hosts, at the deepest level [tay2024code]"

claim: Diversity pool: 20 services per operating system.
issue: Passed as services_per_os to the service generator (services.py:257).

claim: Two target hosts in place of five, as in the released experiment code.
issue: As U0592: the release's 2 is total_database, documented as DAP database nodes, not targets.
fix_text: "with two target hosts in place of five, as in" -> "with two database hosts as target hosts in place of five, the number set in"

claim: (placement) Both attackers follow the targeted attack scenario, as in the released code.
issue: The sentence-final cite can be read as covering the targeted scenario; the release runs the general scenario (network_type 1) and ends a run at >25 % hosts compromised (time_network.py:49).
fix_text: move \citep{tay2024code} to after "two target hosts in place of five"

claim: MTDShield is run with Tay's released weights and input code.
issue: Weights file experiments/AI_model/main_network_epsilon_0.5_decay_0.99.h5 is in f13ed49 (git ls-tree); input code is MTDAIOperation.get_state_and_time_series (mtd_ai_operation.py:235-287).

In the release a do-nothing decision skips the timeout (the yield sits inside 'if action > 0'), so the dissertation's change (U1033) alters release behaviour; 'as released' overstates, though the next paragraph discloses the change.
fix_text: "run as released, with his weights and input code" -> "run with his released weights and input code"

claim: (uncited neighbour) In the release, a decision to do nothing stops the clock.
issue: With action 0 the while-loop repeats without a yield, so simulated time does not advance.

claim: (uncited neighbour) As released, the evaluation code reads four inputs before the run, so they are zero at every decision, as in Tay's evaluations.
issue: Evaluation is built in MTDAIOperation.__init__ at t = 0 and get_record() returns a fresh DataFrame (attack_statistics.py:45), so host_compromise_ratio, overall_asr_avg, overall_mttc_avg and mtd_freq read 0. Same at f13ed49.

claim: (uncited neighbour) The agent has eight inputs.
issue: The agent has 11 inputs: 8 static and 3 time-series. Two of the four frozen inputs are time-series (mtd_freq, overall_mttc_avg), so 'four of its eight' is a wrong count.
fix_text: "four of its eight inputs" -> "four of its eleven inputs"

claim: Training settings from the release's training script: 100 hosts, new network each episode, 5 000 s per episode, 200 s interval.
issue: new_network=True builds a fresh TimeNetwork every episode (run.py:440-447).

claim: It chooses among complete topology shuffle, IP shuffle, OS diversity and service diversity, or nothing.
issue: action_size = 5 (train_models.py:36); action k registers strategy k-1 (mtd_scheme.py:110); 0 = nothing.

claim: It is told the attacker's current attack action at every decision.
issue: Sensitivity 1 makes random.random() <= 1 always true, so attack type is read at every decision (mtd_ai_operation.py:240-245; evaluation default attacker_sensitivity=1, run.py:193). Unlisted processes read as 7.

claim: A deployment is forced after 2 000 s without one, in both training and the runs.
issue: Mechanism differs: training re-draws the agent's choice until non-zero; evaluation forces action 1, complete topology shuffle (mtd_ai_operation.py:87-88). The caption's 'a deployment is forced' holds for both.
